Tera Kalma Gowan Baba Minu Bemar Banaya
Teri Zahra Nu Lokaan Darbar Bola Ke Haye Bohat Rawaya
Mere Bohay Utton Tur Ke Ewein Guzrey Loki
Kadi Pehlu Taun Apne Main Sajdiyaan Wich V Haye Hath Nahin Chaya
Tere Badoon Main Samajh Gayi Kinu Kehnday Peshi
Tere Shehar De Lokaan Ne Mainu Pak Madine Wich Sham Wakhaya
Jay Esayi Oh Mubahlay Walay Aithay Honday
Main Mar Jandi Baba Jadon Kalma Gowaan Dar Mere Te Giraya
Mainu Hakim Ayho Aakhay Tainu Masla Bhuliya
Iss Gal Ne Zahra Nu Main Deen Di Waris Nu Mar Mukaya
Piyo Di Turbat Uttay AKBAR Ayho Aakhay Bibi
Mainu Dhiyaan Te Putraan Aj Waang Yateema Haye Seene Lagaya

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
path = 'src/data/lyrics/tera-kalma-gowan-baba-minu-bemar-banaya.md'
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + path], text=True).split('---', 2)[2].strip().splitlines()
_, metadata, body = Path(path).read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = metadata.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1].splitlines()
source = body.strip().splitlines()
assert roman[0] == '  1' and source[0] == '۱'
assert [line.strip().casefold() for line in roman[1:]] == [line.casefold() for line in old]
assert len(source[1:]) == len(old) == 12
assert all(any('\\u0600' <= ch <= '\\u06ff' for ch in line) for line in source[1:])
assert '\\u200c' not in body
PY

item.text:
Reconstructed all 12 verses in Shahmukhi Punjabi. The grammar throughout supports Punjabi, so I updated the language metadata and removed the missing-source tag.

I preserved the Roman wording and order in `romanLyrics`, adjusted capitalization, and verified that both versions have 12 verse lines in one numbered block. I read the ambiguous Roman `chaya` as `چایا`, meaning “lifted” in context.
